headings.title: SMTO-SKL-0073 — SMTO couldn't find that OneDrive or SharePoint item

html:
SMTO-SKL-0073 — SMTO couldn't find that OneDrive or SharePoint item

GUID: 8bfc0da9-f521-5239-b6d5-ed1d3ce63673
Slug: microsoft365-file-not-found
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • Microsoft says the file, folder or library SMTO asked for doesn't exist for this account. It may have been moved, renamed or deleted, or it belongs to someone else. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open OneDrive or the SharePoint library in your browser with the same Microsoft account and check that the file or folder is still there. If it was moved, renamed or deleted, SMTO's saved reference to it no longer works.
  2. Ask SMTO in a conversation to search for the file again by its name, then repeat your request. A fresh search gives SMTO the item's current location instead of an outdated one.
  3. If the file belongs to someone else, ask them to share it with the Microsoft account connected to SMTO. Microsoft hides items you can't access, so they look as if they don't exist.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finds the file and completes your request.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO's Microsoft 365 setup. Don't switch SMTO to a different Microsoft account just to find the file.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Microsoft Graph returned 404 (or ErrorItemNotFound) for a file, folder, drive or site operation, and Microsoft365Service.execute mapped resource_not_found to the file family.

What this means

  • A resource-not-found response outside mail/calendar/contact families is translated to the file-not-found family. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • A resource-not-found response outside mail/calendar/contact families is translated to the file-not-found family.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the actual route, account, drive/site scope and exact item ID.

How to fix it

  • Re-resolve the target under the same account_ref with microsoft365.file_search, file_list or drives (and sites_search for SharePoint), then retry with the current exact drive_id, site_id and item_id. Do not substitute another account or tenant; a 404 can also mean the signed-in user cannot see the item.
  • Read/search the same account again and use an exact current resource ID; do not substitute another account or tenant.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended accessible resource is read under the same identity.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
